AI ANALYSIS

Data-Driven Betting Insights

Cameron Young returns to Sedgefield Country Club as the defending champion with the field's best SG Total (+1.97) and SG Approach (+0.80), commanding a 9.5% model win probability that towers over the rest of the field. Aaron Rai, the 2024 champion, profiles as perhaps the strongest course fit play in the entire field at +0.402, combining elite ball-striking (4th in SG Approach at +0.56) with back-to-back top-5 finishes at this venue. Further down the board, Mac Meissner (+6022) stands out as a compelling longshot with a 16.0% top-10 probability and +0.92 SG Total — a stronger model projection than several players priced well above him.
Young's Dominant Profile Justifies Favoritism
Cameron Young leads the field in SG Total (+1.97, nearly half a stroke clear of second-ranked Justin Thomas at +1.32) and SG Approach (+0.80). His 9.5% model win probability is nearly triple the next closest player, and his defending title at Sedgefield Country Club (1st in 2025, T22 in 2024) confirms he thrives on this layout.
Cameron Young
Rai's Course Fit Is Off the Charts
Aaron Rai's +0.402 course fit score is the highest in the entire field by a massive margin, and his Sedgefield Country Club history reads 1st (2024) and T5 (2025). The model gives him a 21.4% top-10 probability and 2.8% win probability, driven by his elite SG Approach (+0.56, 4th in field) matching perfectly with what this course demands.
Aaron Rai
Koivun's Projection Belies Limited History
Jackson Koivun sits second in the model at 3.9% win probability despite having only one start at Sedgefield Country Club (T5 in 2025). His +0.084 course fit is solid and his profile clearly impresses the model, but bettors should weigh the small sample of course history against the aggressive projection.
Jackson Koivun
Griffin Combines Putting With Course Pedigree
Ben Griffin ranks 4th in the field in SG Putting (+0.44) and owns the best course history adjustment among serious contenders at +0.075 strokes, built on finishes of T11 (2025) and T7 (2024) at Sedgefield Country Club. The model gives him a 22.3% top-10 probability and 3.1% win chance, making him one of the most well-rounded profiles in this tier.
Ben Griffin
Thomas Brings Elite Strokes Gained, Thin History
Justin Thomas ranks 2nd in the field in SG Total (+1.32) but has just one Sedgefield Country Club start (T12 in 2023) and a slightly negative course fit (-0.035). The model projects him at 2.7% to win and 19.9% for a top 10 — a profile powered almost entirely by raw ball-striking talent rather than course-specific advantages.
Justin Thomas
Meissner Leads Longshot Value Profiles
At +6022, Mac Meissner carries a 16.0% top-10 projection — the highest of any player priced +6000 or longer — and a +0.92 SG Total that ranks 11th in the field, better than five players priced shorter than him. The course record backs it up: a runner-up finish at Sedgefield in 2025 and a T12 in 2024 make him the model's top pick in the deep longshot tier.
Mac Meissner
McNealy's Putter Fuels Sleeper Profile
Maverick McNealy leads the entire field in SG Putting (+0.53) and carries a strong +1.17 SG Total, yet his -0.125 course fit and -0.030 course history adjustment introduce real concerns about his Sedgefield Country Club suitability. The model still projects him at 15.4% for a top 10 at +5410, a profile driven by flatstick dominance that could overcome fit concerns if his iron play holds up.
Maverick McNealy
Fitzpatrick: Under-the-Radar Ball-Striker
Alex Fitzpatrick ranks 3rd in the field in SG Approach (+0.67) with a +1.09 SG Total and positive course fit (+0.125). The model projects a 17.6% top-10 probability at +4669 — a strong mid-tier profile built on the approach-game prowess that Sedgefield Country Club historically rewards.
Alex Fitzpatrick
Bradley's All-Around Game Fits the Tier
Keegan Bradley at +5450 carries a 15.8% model top-10 probability with +0.98 SG Total, placing him as one of the strongest overall profiles in the 50/1-plus range. His well-rounded strokes gained profile lacks a glaring weakness, which suits a Sedgefield Country Club layout that doesn't overwhelmingly favor one skill.
Keegan Bradley
Simpson's History Can't Overcome Current Form
Webb Simpson owns the field's best course history adjustment (+0.204 strokes) at Sedgefield Country Club, but at +62400 the model projects just a fraction of a percent win probability. His current form simply cannot support the weight of past glory — a classic nostalgia trap for bettors at this venue.
Webb Simpson
